scope: Manual theorem, preregistration and implementation review. No native census replay, raw TSV query, source-corpus or phoneme-key fit; no native result counts consulted.
proof_checks: For a source-word-final consonant C, no following vowel exists, so the final forward step is the bare-C branch emitting cc. Earlier steps cannot remove these final two units.
The implication is only source-final-C => equal final output units. C A C A under inherent vowel A also emits cc and ends in a vowel, so the converse fails.

For one fixed key only 17 working units may be consonant bodies. Summing the 17 largest strict terminal-double counts is a valid generous maximum over all such subsets. The complement formula D minus the five smallest counts is identical.
M/N bounds the consonant-final fraction only among strict complete groups under the fixed one-source-word/one-output-group and working-unit contract.

(M+U)/(N+U) is conservative if every excluded stored raw group is one source word: at most M strict words and at most all U excluded words can be consonant-final. The unknown groups need not be jointly realizable, so this is an upper bound rather than an achievable fit. Different actual source-word counts invalidate this extended denominator.
implementation_checks: Primary tokenizer takes complete longest working units; validator independently matches fixed full units and rejects any unmatched raw content. The specified inventory has no alternate complete segmentation from its shorter s branch because h is not a standalone unit.
Double classification compares the last two complete working units, not the last two ASCII characters; one-unit groups are not counted.
Both seam and parse failures are excluded from strict N and retained in U with separate reason counts. No uncertain form is normalized or silently dropped from total accounting.

GDT1342 source-builder code filters kind P after a selector-first guarded query; its source validator reconstructs that complete P projection. GDT1343 reuses the pinned SOURCE bytes and validator checks the 179-selector allowlist and sealed-page exclusions.
Primary checks unique input IDs; validator compares every saved classification and all witness records and uses the independent complement form of the 17-body arithmetic.
No source-language threshold, specific consonant/vowel key or positive model-fit decision is inferred by the scripts.
limits: This review does not independently recollate original manuscript pixels or prove transcription, word boundaries or phonetic units.
The frozen validator checks the stored converse fixture but does not independently reconstruct the entire source-free encoding enumeration; the terminal theorem was reviewed directly here.
No claim that a low capacity excludes a language or all default-vowel constructions is justified. It constrains only the declared doubling rule and source-word/group binding.
No assertion here that the separately running census or executable validator has completed.
